prompt:
A full-body character image, vertical 2:3 (1024×1536): Yu Ji of the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, reimagined as an adult woman — the Taoist who vanished before Sun Ce's eyes.

1. STYLE
Korean MMORPG character artwork. A recognisably drawn face with gently simplified anatomical structure. 2D painting with visible brushwork: layered strokes of colour, soft broken edges, thin coloured linework and a few crisp accents on the face and costume.
Her face is small and soft: a short midface, a softly rounded jaw and a small chin, about 1.3 times as long as it is wide, with her eyes open at their natural size. Bangs, side locks and headpieces frame the face without lengthening it.
Skin finish: dewy, glass-like highlights on the skin of her shoulders, arms, collarbones and legs — a soft, luminous wet-look sheen that follows the body's forms; her face keeps a soft, natural finish.

2. CHARACTER
Age: mid-twenties — a clear adult face.
Face — her own, recognisably this character, a woman's face with no beard or facial hair: a clear, innocent purity; porcelain-pale skin; heart-shaped face; smaller, narrower eyes than usual anime proportion — narrow upturned eyes, outer eye corners slightly lifted; thin arched brows; small button nose; thin lips with a defined cupid's bow; teal eyes; glossy nude lips.
Body and hair: slender-limbed yet full-busted with rounded hips and a narrow waist build; very long loose mermaid waves to the waist with curtain bangs; pale jade-green hair.
Expression: a relaxed, unforced face, lips gently closed, subtle and relaxed.
Legend, carried in her design and bearing: ethereal mystic calm, white robes, drifting mist.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME AND EQUIPMENT — MEDIEVAL FANTASY
Costume: a royal chancellor's or court scholar's dress — a long embroidered coat with a stole, a seal ring, ledgers and a quill. Western medieval high-fantasy dress — plate, mail and heraldic tabards, gowns and mantles, circlets and crowns; steel, leather, wool, velvet and gold, with a subtle magical glow along the patterns. Her Three Kingdoms origin shows through her signature item, her colours and her bearing.
Silhouette: thin leaf-patterned armor plates and flowing light fabric panels with a slender circlet — a slender, graceful silhouette. This silhouette sets the overall shape of the costume above — keep its materials, ornaments and rank in this shape; the details are free.
Colours: undyed linen white, bamboo green, ink grey and pale celadon.
Signature item: a Taoist horsetail whisk, reimagined as a Western high-fantasy version of the same kind of object with the same silhouette — polished steel and silvered mithril throughout, the shaft or hilt also forged metal with engraved runes (never plain wood), a faint magical glow running along the edge and the runes, a gem-set guard or socket, a leather-wrapped grip and heraldic or elven ornament, with any animal motif re-sculpted in Western heraldic style. She holds it at full scale: one whole object, drawn once, held in front of or beside her body; a long weapon keeps one straight, unbroken shaft with a single head or blade.
Exposure (bold): her regalia opens to show skin — bare upper arms below the pauldrons, which stay seated on top of her shoulders (bare shoulders only where no shoulder guard sits), a deep open neckline under the gorget with natural cleavage, the tabard or gown cut with a high side slit at full length — it shows the side line of one leg as she stands, no leg pushed out or knee bent for it; armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: the shattered realms of medieval high fantasy, an age of rival warlords after a fallen empire: a ruined imperial capital, mercenary camps, border keeps, outlaw marches and wild southern jungles, dark violet battle-magic.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: a soft key light with a strong rim light tracing her hair, shoulders and armour; bright, crisp specular highlights on metal and jewellery, and a clean, warm-neutral sheen on her skin.
Composition: her whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet inside the frame with clear margins, about four-fifths of the image height; camera at chest height with natural portrait perspective.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only — no second character, horse or other creature. No readable text or numbers — banners and shields carry only heraldic devices (a beast or a crest), never letters or Chinese characters. No logo, watermark, speech bubble or frame border. A Western medieval setting and dress only — stone castles, Romanesque or Gothic architecture — with no Chinese architecture, robes or hanzi.
Avoid: a blue or bruise-like tint on the skin around the eyes, glossy or shiny highlights on the face, sweaty, oily or plastic-looking skin.

Costume design: a floor-length priestly vestment with gold-trimmed stoles and a tall head ornament — a long devout silhouette. Signature construction: successive half-arches cut into the rigid shoulder mantle and stoles diminish into airy open gaps, echoing a saint who vanishes from sight. Ivory wool, bamboo-green velvet, celadon silk and ink-grey metal with fine silver and gold details. A deep neckline, bare upper arms and high slit show skin; intimate areas covered.

Weapon (fixed — ours): a Taoist horsetail whisk, reimagined as a Western high-fantasy version of the same kind of object with the same silhouette: polished steel and silvered mithril throughout, the shaft or hilt also forged metal with engraved runes (never plain wood), a faint magical glow running along the edge and the runes, a gem-set guard or socket, a leather-wrapped grip and heraldic or elven ornament, with any animal motif re-sculpted in Western heraldic style and no Chinese fittings, silk tassels or hanzi.

Hair colour (fixed — ours): pale jade-green hair. Keep exactly this hair colour; only the hairstyle is yours.

Skin tone (fixed — ours): porcelain-pale skin. Keep exactly this skin tone.

Costume colours (ours): undyed linen white, bamboo green, ink grey and pale celadon.

Rank (fixed): she is a high court official — her costume must read dignified office at first glance: refined, layered and finely ornamented, with flagship-card detail, never plain or sparse.

Exposure (fixed): bold — her outfit shows skin by design (a deep neckline, bare shoulders or arms, a high slit or short hem); intimate areas covered.

Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin — never a long face or a long, pointed or heavy jaw; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline and never lengthens her face. Her eyes stay at a natural open size — never squeezed into narrow slits.

Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her crown or headpiece to both boots stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every genre; her hands and her signature item stay inside the frame. Camera at chest height with natural portrait perspective — no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

Pose and setting: standing in a deserted Gothic cloister herb garden at morning, torso facing forward, her head turned only slightly toward the viewer, holding the complete mithril horsetail whisk beside her right shoulder while the left hand rests open over her heart; thin silver magical mist drifting through the arches.

One figure only, natural hands with five fingers; Western medieval setting and dress only — no Chinese architecture, robes, junks or hanzi; no logo or watermark.
